# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

<!-- cap-evolve:framework-improvements-append-below -->

## From cand_0003 (tau2 airline run)

- **The gate and the trial budget fight each other, and the proposer can't tell.** With hill-climb:all at ~2·SE and only 3 trials/task, a candidate can raise the val mean by +0.10–0.12 with ZERO regressions across TWO straight iterations and still be rejected every time, because no single task crosses 2·SE. The RESULT line correctly says "lever is POWER or SIZE," but the proposer has no way to know whether the right response is "make the edit bigger" or "the edit is already right, you just need more trials to resolve it." Suggestion: when a rejected candidate has Δmean > 0 AND broke={} AND fixed={} for N consecutive iterations, have the framework surface a note like "effect positive and non-damaging but under-resolved; consider raising trials/task" — or auto-escalate the trial count for the next evaluation. Otherwise every late iteration burns itself re-deriving "this is a measurement-power plateau" from the journal.

- **`unresolved={...}` is easy to misread as "these tasks were touched."** The RESULT text already warns "NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks," but the set still looks like a damage/attribution list. A clearer field name (e.g. `under_resolved_at_2SE={...}`) or splitting it into `moved_positive_subthreshold` / `moved_negative_subthreshold` would stop proposers from redesigning on noise.

- **tau2 is not importable from the candidate working dir**, so verifying an in-body guard means replaying the engine's arithmetic by hand against trace arguments (I read the tau2 source on disk and reproduced it in a standalone script). A tiny read-only `verify/` harness that imports the real domain engine and lets the proposer dry-run a tool call against a task's initial DB — without consuming an eval trial — would make guard verification exact instead of reconstructed, and is strictly cheaper than a wrong candidate.
